races.name: Welcome To Family Day Juvenile Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Tiny Riot
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton teams up with Dan Skelton's lightly-raced three-year-old who has won and placed on good ground over 16f, making this 2m½f trip an interesting stamina test; a natural hold-up runner with sound recent form, 30 days since last run is no concern.

runners_data.name: Hello Garda
runners_data.note: Paddy Hanlon (claimer) takes the ride for John Joseph Hanlon, whose 14-day strike rate is zero from 11 runners; this horse's flat form shows consistent fading in the finish, and while it holds up naturally at the rear, it has been pushed into a midfield slot by the crowded hold-up field, which further tempers its finishing prospects.

runners_data.name: Just Call Me Mo
runners_data.note: Absent 76 days (flagged) for Joseph Parr, whose 14-day return is a thin 0/1; all five career runs have come at Stratford on Soft or Standard surfaces, making this Good to Firm ground a genuine concern, and the horse has never finished better than sixth — its natural rear-running style is squeezed further by redistribution into midfield.

runners_data.name: Lucky Sevens
runners_data.note: Jonathan Burke rides for James Owen (10/57 in 14 days, solid stable form), and this horse's record of 2W4P from 10 good-ground runs is the strongest going-specific profile in the field; placed last time out 13 days ago over 16f on good ground, it is battle-hardened and well-suited to this fast-ground sprint shape.

races.paceDynamic: With all four runners carrying a hold-up profile and no confirmed front-runner in the field, this race at Stratford over 2m½f on Good to Firm ground is likely to produce a dawdling early pace as each jockey waits for a rival to commit. The field is likely to crawl through the early stages before coiling into a sprint finish from the final hurdle, a shape that classically suits the horse with the most finishing kick and jump fluency at the death. Tiny Riot and Lucky Sevens are the two with the strongest recent form credentials to exploit such a finish, both having placed or won off comparable pace scenarios on good ground. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the map can cleanly place at the rear — Hello Garda and Just Call Me Mo are redistributed to midfield, but both are true closers who may actually find themselves forced to race slightly closer to the pace than they'd prefer, reducing their effectiveness as late finishers. This race shape — a slow-run, sprint-to-the-line contest — overwhelmingly favours the horse with the sharpest turn of foot and the soundest jumping in the final quarter-mile, giving the advantage to runners with proven good-ground speed and recent competitive form.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish From Tape
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow throughout and the race reduces to a flat-out sprint from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: With no natural leader, the field idles in a tight bunch before exploding into a furious finish, rewarding the horse with the cleanest jump at the last and the sharpest acceleration on fast ground. Tiny Riot and Lucky Sevens both have the good-ground form and recent competitive runs to dominate this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Runner Breaks Early
scenarios.trigger: If one jockey takes the initiative and sets an uncontested lead from the outset, controlling tempo through the hurdles.
scenarios.body: A solo leader drags the field into a more honest gallop, stretching the closers and testing their jumping rhythm over the 2m½f trip on fast ground. Lucky Sevens, with experience of front-position racing and a string of placed efforts, could track and pounce, while Tiny Riot's hold-up style might see it finish strongly from behind.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate rather than funereal and the genuine hold-up types can find daylight approaching the final flight.
scenarios.body: A sustainable gallop allows Hello Garda and Just Call Me Mo to travel within themselves before unleashing their finishes, though both carry a STYLE_FIT discount having been mapped out of their natural rear positions. Hello Garda's consistent placed efforts on good ground give it the edge in this shape if it can access its preferred late-run role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition On Fast Ground
scenarios.trigger: If the Good to Firm conditions prove taxing enough to cause jumping errors or fatigue, turning the race into a test of stamina and soundness.
scenarios.body: Fast ground over this trip can expose horses with jumping flaws or stamina limitations, potentially eliminating one or more rivals through a mistake or fade in the closing stages. Lucky Sevens' consistent placed form and Jonathan Burke's experienced steering give it the best chance of profiting if a rival falters at a crucial flight.

watchPoints.text: Tiny Riot and Lucky Sevens are the two horses most likely to dominate the sprint finish — watch which of Harry Skelton or Jonathan Burke moves first approaching the second-last hurdle, as that move could decide the race.

Just Call Me Mo's 76-day absence combined with a switch to Good to Firm ground (all prior runs on Soft or Standard at Stratford) makes it a significant unknown — watch for any signs of greenness or stiffness in the early stages.

Hello Garda is partnered by a 5lb claimer and has a consistent record of fading in finishes on good ground; if it drifts wide or loses contact turning for home, its chance effectively ends in a sprint scenario.

With no natural front-runner, watch the first three hurdles — if the field idles to a near-walk, the eventual winning margin will be tight and jumping at the final flight will be decisive; a clean leap there from any runner could be the winning move.

races.name: Next Sunday Is Ladies Day Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Brionywells
runners_data.note: Won twice over 20-23f on Good ground recently giving her strong form credentials for this trip and surface; a natural hold-up horse for Nick Slatter (3lb claim), she has the course-relevant profile to benefit most from a sprint finish and has placed in five of eleven runs on similar going.

runners_data.name: Stavanger Rose
runners_data.note: Tabitha Worsley takes the ride on this lightly-campaigned mare who has shown nothing but modest form in recent runs including a fall and unseated; her hold-up style suits a slow-run race but the 0W0P record on similar going is a serious concern over a punishing 2m6f trip.

runners_data.name: Bits Ballou
runners_data.note: Sam Twiston-Davies links up with the Twiston-Davies yard who are 0/13 in the past 14 days — a note of caution on stable form; this horse is a genuine deep closer who will be competing for the same late ground as every other runner, and with STYLE_FIT of 0.90, the chance it secures its ideal position is reduced.

runners_data.name: Son Of Tyran
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton is a key booking for Dan Skelton (11/26 in 14 days) and Son Of Tyran's winning run over 24f on Good ground is directly relevant here; wears a bridle, has shown a tendency to fade in finishes, but the top-jockey/trainer combination gives it the best chance of manufacturing a forward position in a leaderless race.

runners_data.name: French Diablo
runners_data.note: Max Comley's four-year-old runs in a hood and was placed third over 22f on Good ground 13 days ago — the recent outing is a fitness plus; pushed into the midfield on the map despite being a confirmed hold-up type, its scope at this longer 2m6f trip on quick ground is unproven and the 0W1P similar-going record is thin.

runners_data.name: Babychino
runners_data.note: Ms Sophie Carter rides with a 7lb claim for Alexander Gibbons (0/1 in 14 days); this four-year-old has been placed at 20f and 16f on Good ground but the step up to 2m6f is a significant stamina question, and being mapped ahead of its natural position reduces the chance it can produce its best late run.

runners_data.name: League Clash
runners_data.note: 671 days off the track is the standout flag here — Sheila Lewis's gelding wore a tongue-tie in its last run and has form over 26f on Good ground including a third, which is the most relevant trip profile in the field; the long absence makes fitness the dominant concern, though the trip experience is genuine.

runners_data.name: Pink Walls
runners_data.note: Michael Mullineaux's six-year-old runs in a hood and has the lowest OR in the field at 62, with a 0W0P record across 13 runs on similar going and a form string of P0-P8; Kevin Brogan takes the ride but the evidence across every angle — form, class, going, trip — points to this being a race-fitness run rather than a winning threat.

races.paceDynamic: This 2m6f Good to Firm test at Stratford is a genuinely unusual puzzle: every single runner in the field carries a hold-up style profile, meaning there is no confirmed front-runner to set a tempo and the early gallop could be almost comically slow before the field suddenly quickens heading to the final hurdles. With Brionywells and Stavanger Rose the only two horses not flagged as redistributed, the pace map confirms these two are the natural rearmost types, while Bits Ballou, Son Of Tyran, French Diablo, Babychino, League Clash and Pink Walls are all genuine hold-up horses who have been pushed into the midfield slots purely because the map has nowhere else to put them. The race will almost certainly be run at a crawl through the early stages before a messy, bunched sprint develops from two out, creating a genuinely lottery-like finish with position, luck in running and jumping accuracy likely to matter more than pure class. The shape overwhelmingly favours horses with a sharp jump of a hurdle and an ability to quicken from a compressed pack — those with course-relevant form on Good to Firm ground and a jockey able to manufacture a position in a muddled, slow-run heat will hold the clearest advantage; Son Of Tyran and Brionywells profile most naturally for this shape given their recent good-ground form at longer trips. The field holds more hold-up types than can all genuinely settle at the rear — of those remapped to midfield, Son Of Tyran (Harry Skelton) and Bits Ballou (Sam Twiston-Davies) are most likely to actually secure a forward pitch in the absence of any true front-runner.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Gallop Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If no horse assumes control and a crawling early pace produces a bunched finish from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: With the entire field comprising hold-up types, the tempo will be almost non-existent until the final mile, compressing runners into a group and making jumping accuracy at the final two hurdles the decisive factor.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Reluctant Leader Cracks Late
scenarios.trigger: If one redistributed horse is bounced into a brief lead early but fades under pressure from the home turn.
scenarios.body: A horse like Bits Ballou or Son Of Tyran, pushed forward by their jockey in a vacuum, sets a modest pace but is vulnerable to those tracking off the bridle — stay-on types who relish the longer trip get first run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Big Outsider Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse at long odds is given a charmed passage through the compressed pack and catches leaders flat-footed at the last.
scenarios.body: Good to Firm ground and the longer 2m6f trip suit a horse that has shown stamina at this trip — League Clash's third over 26f and French Diablo's recent third over 22f in similar conditions give them each a credible late profile.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If two horses break well and immediately set a stronger-than-expected gallop that stretches the field before the final bend.
scenarios.body: In this scenario the hold-up horses are disadvantaged and unable to close, leaving those who accidentally lead or sit a close second in a strong position at the last — Stavanger Rose and Babychino, both placed at similar distances, could benefit.

watchPoints.text: Son Of Tyran wears a bridle and has a noted tendency to fade in the finish — watch whether Harry Skelton can hold his position until the last possible moment before asking for an effort, as any early move in a sprint finish will expose the horse's stamina limitation.

League Clash is 671 days absent — watch the paddock and early jumping closely for any sign of ring rustiness, as a horse with that layoff can either come fresh and dangerous or make jumping errors that end its race early.

With no genuine front-runner, watch whether any horse is accidentally bounced into a reluctant lead in the first mile — if Bits Ballou or Son Of Tyran end up setting a pace they are not built to sustain, the complexion of the entire race changes.
Pink Walls has pulled up twice in its last four runs and runs in a hood — watch how it jumps the early hurdles as another jumping failure would confirm it is simply not firing this season.

Brionywells has won twice in her last four runs on Good ground and is 2W2P from 11 similar-going runs — her recent form is the strongest in the field and worth tracking from the flag to see whether Nick Slatter can manufacture a clear run in what will be a compressed, traffic-heavy finish.

races.name: Gary Hubball's 60th Celebration Year Novices' Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Laffer Curve
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton in the saddle for Dan Skelton's yard, which is firing at 13/29 over the past 14 days — a powerful combination; races prominently and is versatile enough to track Aslukgoes throughout, with good-ground form (5/8 in similar conditions) and five recent runs all within easy striking range of the lead.

runners_data.name: Aslukgoes
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, set to enjoy a completely uncontested lead on good-to-firm ground, but the OR=99 and a recent unseated rider on the form string raises jumping questions; Mickey Bowen's eight-year-old is likely to get a dream trip in front but its ability to sustain it over 2m6½f on quick ground is the key risk.

runners_data.name: Artiste D'ainay
runners_data.note: Billy Aprahamian's eight-year-old has won over 24f on good ground and has strong prominent-racing credentials; races in tongue tie, holds a course-compatible profile, and should sit just off Aslukgoes, but a return of 0/1 for the trainer over the past 14 days is a minor flag.

runners_data.name: Royal Time
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor takes the ride on Shane Crawley's hold-up operator who has genuine form over this trip (including a run over 26f); the 52-day absence is worth noting, but a previous second over 26f good ground suggests he handles the conditions, and he is the most credible natural closer in the race.

runners_data.name: My Lovely Horse
runners_data.note: David Bridgwater's six-year-old races off OR=75 with an amateur apprentice, James Turner (5), and hold-up form that has not translated into a win or place on this type of ground — sim-going record of 0W/0P in three runs; the tongue tie points to a tendency to idle, and this looks a tough task.

runners_data.name: Frankie Faulkner
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type by inclination — Mrs Williams' nine-year-old has placed off hold-up tactics on softer ground — but with several horses already filling the rear, it will struggle to get its true position and the 67-day layoff adds an extra question mark at OR=73.

runners_data.name: Shuile Warrior
runners_data.note: Simon Edwards' eight-year-old is 85 days off the track and its entire recent form book is on soft or heavy ground; the single run on good going (sim-going: 1/5) offers almost no confidence it handles this surface, making it hard to assess positively regardless of pace shape.

runners_data.name: Rockvale
runners_data.note: Sam Allwood's seven-year-old has placed at 21f on good ground and showed a second over 21f in similar conditions, so the trip and surface are not concerns; however it is a true hold-up horse pushed forward on the map by congestion at the rear, meaning it will likely race closer than ideal to its natural style without the natural rhythm that brings out its best.

runners_data.name: Miss Pearl
runners_data.note: David Rees' ten-year-old has shown glimpses of form — a third over 20f good ground recently — and wears a tongue tie, but age and modest OR=72 are against it; a genuine hold-up operator by nature, it is mapped to midfield only because there is no room at the rear, and the resulting compromise in running style weakens its prospects materially.

runners_data.name: Citizen Jane
runners_data.note: Ryan Potter's five-year-old has won twice over 20f on good ground (/11) which gives the form-based case some credibility, but its entire placed form comes on soft or heavy; a natural come-from-behind type placed mid-field by congestion, it will likely race out of its preferred zone — the style compromise and surface switch from soft to good-to-firm represent compounding risks at OR=71.

races.paceDynamic: Aslukgoes is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner novices' handicap chase over 2m6½f on good-to-firm ground at Stratford, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Mickey Bowen's eight-year-old should dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo from the front — a pace that is likely to be sustainable rather than scorching, suiting those who can travel comfortably behind and produce a clean jump at the last. Artiste D'ainay is the most natural prominent type to track the leader, while Laffer Curve — a consistent sort from the Dan Skelton yard — should also be forward enough to exploit the moderate gallop. The field contains significantly more hold-up types than can realistically get their preferred position at the rear; Rockvale, Frankie Faulkner, Miss Pearl, and Citizen Jane are all mapped forward of their natural station, and none can be expected to be finishing from as far back as they ideally want. A controlled, single-file pace set by Aslukgoes over this stamina-demanding trip strongly favours prominent racers who jump fluently and travel into the race — horses with enough class to keep tabs on the front-runner and quicken modestly at the business end will be at a premium.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Aslukgoes Controls; Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Aslukgoes leads unchallenged and sets an honest but manageable tempo that rewards those racing prominently behind.
scenarios.body: Aslukgoes dictates from the front with Artiste D'ainay and Laffer Curve the likeliest to track, and the race becomes a test of jumping accuracy and class from the front two-thirds of the field over the final mile; the stable form of the Skelton runner and the course form of Artiste D'ainay make them the prime beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Aslukgoes Fades; Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Aslukgoes has shot its bolt jumping the last two fences and a close-tracking rival swoops to lead on the run-in.
scenarios.body: The front-runner's recent form — including a U on its latest start — raises the question of jumping reliability, and a prominent tracker who has been economical through the race collects as the leader tires; Laffer Curve's consistency from a prominent pitch makes it the natural heir in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or a melee at a fence breaks the race wide open and creates a late-run opportunity from further back.
scenarios.body: This scenario demands a genuine closing move, yet most of the apparent hold-up types here are redistributed from their natural positions and unlikely to be ridden truly cold; Royal Time, handled by Jack Tudor, is the most credible natural hold-up horse in the field and the best-placed to exploit any late gaps.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace; Messy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the uncontested pace is so steady that the field concertinas at the last fence and the result becomes a jumping lottery.
scenarios.body: A very slow tempo over this stamina trip would compress the field, making errors at the final fences decisive and randomising the finish; Citizen Jane and Miss Pearl lack the experience and OR quality to win neatly, but a blunder from a rival could elevate them in a muddled conclusion.

watchPoints.text: Aslukgoes (Harry Reed) — watch whether it stands up and jumps cleanly throughout; its last run ended in an unseated rider and if it makes a jumping error mid-race, the entire pace scenario unravels and a tracker will inherit the lead on much better terms.

Laffer Curve (Harry Skelton) — monitor its position jumping the fourth-last; if it is sitting comfortably on the shoulder of Aslukgoes at that point with a clear round, the Skelton team momentum and in-form trainer give it a major each-way claim and it will be hard to beat.

Royal Time (Jack Tudor) — coming back from 52 days off, watch for any sluggishness early or signs of ring-rustiness in the first mile; if Tudor can place him handily without using energy, the trip and going profile make him a live threat in the final half-mile.

Rockvale and Miss Pearl — both true hold-up horses being effectively forced to race out of their preferred zone by field congestion; if either is seen fighting for position in the first half-mile rather than settling, their finishing kick in the closing stages is likely to be compromised significantly.

races.name: University Hospitals Birmingham Charity Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Gambino
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's five-year-old has the race entirely on his terms as the lone front-runner; his two placings and one win on good-to-similar ground are directly relevant here, and Harry Skelton can set whatever tempo suits — the style-fit flag relates to being mapped as prominent rather than lead, but in practice he will be on the front end from flag-fall.

runners_data.name: Haderach
runners_data.note: Stephen Allen's five-year-old has a troubling form string of pulled-ups and unseated on recent runs, and carries the ⚠ fades-in-finish flag; no trainer activity in the last 14 days, 68 days off, and a hurdles history that reads poorly on good ground make this one of the weaker profiles in the field.

runners_data.name: Penzance
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse placed at the rear of this map by redistribution — he's been in good heart recently with back-to-back seconds on good ground over staying trips, and the 12-day turnaround is quick but connections clearly think he's ready; the apprentice claim of Paddy Hanlon (5lb) is relevant for weight purposes.

runners_data.name: Usyk
runners_data.note: Nigel and Willy Twiston-Davies's five-year-old has repeatedly contested staying-trip races on good ground without converting, with a best recent effort of second over 16f; Miss Amber Jackson-Fennell claims 7lb but the form string of 26-45O shows consistent underperformance, and good-to-firm conditions have not unlocked anything new yet.

runners_data.name: Delgany Second Now
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's four-year-old — stablemate of Gambino — has produced three consecutive finishes outside the top five and his form over 16-18f on good ground is modest at best; pushed into a midfield map position from a true hold-up profile, the 11-day turnaround and a form line of 5-77 do not inspire confidence at this level.

runners_data.name: Genealogy
runners_data.note: Faye Bramley's four-year-old has the most credible hold-up credentials in this field, with a recent second over 16f on good ground and Harry Cobden booked for the ride — a jockey upgrade that carries genuine significance; his style-fit adjustment is minor (0.93) compared to others, and he's the most natural beneficiary if Gambino's lead is reeled in late.

runners_data.name: Angel Of My Dreams
runners_data.note: David Killahena & Graeme McPherson's five-year-old is flagged as a fader in the finish, which is a significant concern in a steadily-run race where the final two hurdles will be a stern examination; placed second on good ground over 16f suggests talent, but the redistribution away from the rear and the fading flag combine to dampen the scenario in which this horse wins.

races.paceDynamic: Gambino is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner maiden hurdle at Stratford, and with no other genuine pace-pusher to challenge him, Harry Skelton can dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo on good-to-firm ground. The remaining six runners — Haderach, Penzance, Usyk, Delgany Second Now, Genealogy, and Angel Of My Dreams — are all hold-up types by profile, meaning the field will almost certainly string out behind Gambino with no meaningful pressure applied early. This creates a single-file, convoy-style race where the pace is entirely in Gambino's hands, likely producing a steady-to-moderate gallop that rewards those who travel well through the race rather than those who need a genuine end-to-end test. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and pounce at the second-last, and — critically — Gambino himself, who controls every variable from the front. Note that the field holds more true hold-up types than the map can place at the rear; Genealogy, Delgany Second Now, Angel Of My Dreams and Penzance are the most likely to end up in closer-than-natural positions, but only the most tractable among them will secure a genuinely useful pitch behind the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gambino Controls, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Gambino leads uncontested at a measured clip and Skelton times the surge from the second-last perfectly.
scenarios.body: Gambino sets every fraction on his own terms, never hard-ridden until the home straight, and his good-ground form (1W2P on similar going) gives him the engine to repel challengers who haven't travelled as sweetly; a controlled pace also means he doesn't empty out late, neutralising his historical fade risk.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Gambino sets a stronger-than-expected tempo and a hold-up horse tracks the pace efficiently before unleashing a late run.
scenarios.body: A true hold-up performer who travels kindly in the slipstream could benefit if the pace picks up sharply from three out, causing Gambino to tie up close home; Genealogy's recent second on good ground and Harry Cobden's positional intelligence make this the most plausible counter-narrative.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Racer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types manages to secure a prominent position and presses Gambino from the home turn.
scenarios.body: The pace map is crowded with horses racing out of their natural role, and if one — most likely Penzance or Delgany Second Now — gets a clean run into second or third heading to the last, the race becomes a stamina battle on good-to-firm turf that could catch Gambino cold; however, all four redistributed runners carry a style-fit discount, so this scenario requires a degree of tactical fortune.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Gambino is taken on unexpectedly early or makes a serious jumping error, fragmenting the field and producing a messy finish.
scenarios.body: With no natural challenger in the field this is the least likely shape, but a stumble at a hurdle or an unusually aggressive early move from one of the hold-up horses could produce a stop-start gallop that scrambles the form; in that scenario finishing ability and jumping fluency matter above all, and horses with clean hurdles form benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Gambino — watch whether Harry Skelton elects to coast or inject pace at the top of the home straight; if he kicks early and clears, no horse in this field has the profile to close him down.

Genealogy — Harry Cobden will be positioning this horse to travel in the slipstream of Gambino from the third-last; if he gets a clean run between the final two hurdles he is the one most likely to pose a late threat.
Haderach — three non-completions in recent form (pulls-up and unseated) combined with 68 days off; watch at the early hurdles for jumping fluency or signs of jumping-related confidence issues.

Penzance — quick 12-day return for this hold-up horse; monitor how Paddy Hanlon (5) positions him from the gate, as a natural hold-up type nudged forward by redistribution could find himself in unfamiliar traffic in the early stages.

Angel Of My Dreams — the ⚠ fades-in-finish flag combined with the likely steady early pace means the home straight may expose this runner; watch for any drop in fluency between the last two flights where the race will be decided.

races.name: Visit Zoolab In The Centre Course Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Person Of Interest
runners_data.note: Harry Cobden takes over for Faye Bramley's six-year-old who has solid form on Good ground (2 wins, 4 places in 12 comparable runs) but has failed to finish on two recent starts (P, U); a true hold-up horse who will need the race to develop late pace — the uncontested scenario is not ideal but the class margin over the field is real.

runners_data.name: Definite Dream
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner who will dictate from flag to finish; Denis Coakley's eight-year-old has been consistent without winning (0W/5P in similar going) and wears a tongue tie — sustainable pace is his weapon but his inability to win from the front recently raises a genuine question about whether he can hold on.

runners_data.name: Thickthorn Tom
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's six-year-old has Harry Skelton aboard and arrives in career-best form (2-1-2 in last four finishes, including a win over 21f on Good); a hold-up horse who has placed on both Good and Soft, his stamina profile for 2m3½f looks well-suited and the Skelton operation is in red-hot form (T14: 10/27).

runners_data.name: Applejack Poet
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy's nine-year-old ran just seven days ago, which is a freshness flag; a true hold-up horse who is being pushed forward on the map due to field congestion, meaning he will not get his natural position — all 15 runs on similar going show no wins, and the style displacement makes his chance harder to construct.

runners_data.name: Boom Boom
runners_data.note: Rob Summers' eight-year-old wears a tongue tie and recent form reads PP after two wins earlier in the season on Good to Firm — a natural back-marker who has tumbled in the ratings (OR 83) and whose recent pulled-up runs suggest an immediate bounce-back cannot be assumed; mapped mid-field but likely to race at the rear as his instincts dictate.

runners_data.name: Bahtiyar
runners_data.note: Max Young's eight-year-old wears a phood (p headgear) and has been placed six times without winning on Good ground in 14 comparable runs; genuinely holds up off the pace by nature and has been pushed forward by the map's redistribution — the most likely of the displaced hold-up horses to press forward naturally given his better recent form figures (5-2-4-4-2).

runners_data.name: Fox Wallace
runners_data.note: Ella Young's (T14: 0/0) eight-year-old carries the lightest weight (142lbs) and wears a tongue tie; form figures of 6-P-P-P-5 are deeply uninspiring and, as the most natural backmarker in the field with the lowest OR (69), he will drift to the rear regardless of the map position — needs a significant turnaround in jumping reliability to factor.

races.paceDynamic: Definite Dream is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will control the pace from the outset in what shapes up as a truly uncontested, single-paced affair over 2m3½f on Good to Firm ground at Stratford. The six hold-up horses behind — Thickthorn Tom, Person Of Interest, Applejack Poet, Boom Boom, Bahtiyar, and Fox Wallace — will all track from off the pace to varying degrees, meaning the field is stacked with closers and the gallop Definite Dream sets becomes the defining factor. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race map can physically place at the rear; of those redistributed, Applejack Poet and Bahtiyar are the most likely to push forward and secure a prominent position closest to Definite Dream, while Boom Boom and Fox Wallace are more natural back-markers who will drop away regardless. This race shape — one measured, uncontested leader — heavily favours a horse with a strong, relentless galloping profile that can either track and pounce in the final mile or, if the pace is too conservative, the hold-up horses who can sustain a powerful late run; the single biggest advantage goes to those who can sit close enough to Definite Dream to exploit a predictable, controlled tempo without being caught flat-footed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Definite Dream Controlled Dictation
scenarios.trigger: If Definite Dream bowls along unchallenged at a fair but measured clip and no hold-up horse gets close enough to strike.
scenarios.body: Definite Dream settles into a rhythm on good to firm ground, jumps soundly and kicks on from the final turn with no rival able to quicken past; horses that track in second and third position reap the benefit of the steady tempo and arrive with reserves intact.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Poach Race
scenarios.trigger: If Applejack Poet or Bahtiyar push forward to track Definite Dream closely and outgunning the leader at the second-last.
scenarios.body: The prominent positioner gains a ground advantage over the true hold-up horses and arrives at the last with momentum; Definite Dream is collared at the final fence having burned more fuel than anticipated by a closer shadow.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Storm Home
scenarios.trigger: If Definite Dream sets an overly strong gallop that stretches the field and leaves the race wide open for deep closers.
scenarios.body: A fast early pace suits horses who switch off at the back and find a clear run in the straight; Person Of Interest and Thickthorn Tom, both with solid form on similar ground, have the quality to pick up the pieces from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart, Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or fallers disrupt the field and the race becomes a test of pure stamina and jumping accuracy over the final mile.
scenarios.body: With several horses carrying weight concerns and headgear usage in this field, a scrappy, attritional race where bodies fall away hands the advantage to the sounder jumper still standing; Thickthorn Tom's recent win profile over similar trips gives him the edge in a messy contest.

watchPoints.text: Thickthorn Tom — Harry Skelton is in exceptional current form and this horse's recent winning profile over a similar trip on Good ground makes him the primary danger to Definite Dream if he tracks into second approaching the home straight.

Definite Dream's jumping — as the sole front-runner over a chase course, any jumping error or hesitation at a fence will immediately hand the initiative to the horses tracking him, so monitor his jumping at the first three fences to assess whether he is travelling with confidence.

Applejack Poet — ran just seven days ago and, while he is a consistent type on this ground, the quick turnaround combined with his redistribution out of his natural hold-up role means his performance could be significantly compromised if he is forced to race in unfamiliar territory.

Person Of Interest — two non-completions (P, U) in recent starts need explaining before trusting him in a race where the pace shape is unlikely to set up for a late burst; watch whether Cobden positions him more prominently than his profile suggests to compensate for the lack of genuine pace injection mid-race.

Boom Boom — the two pulled-up runs on recent form are a major red flag in a field that does not offer much cover; if he races at the rear and jumps poorly in the early stages, he becomes an in-running risk worth monitoring for a loose horse disruption.

races.name: Try Our Picnic Package Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: War Correspondent
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer for R P Cody who has consistent good-ground form (five place efforts from six similar-going starts) but a patchy recent string including a pulled-up and two unseats — jumping reliability under Paddy Hanlon (5) at this trip needs to hold up for the late effort to count.|

runners_data.name: Donnie Azoff
runners_data.note: Donnie Azoff arrives on the back of a win and a second in his last two starts, both on good ground, and Isabelle Ryder's (5) claim helps offset the 167lbs burden — a genuine hold-up performer with excellent similar-going stats (4 wins from 13) who needs the race not to be completely dawdled through.|

runners_data.name: Snatch A Glance
runners_data.note: Fern O'Brien rides a horse fresh off a 12-day turnaround for Fergal O'Brien; the prominent style is perfectly suited to tracking Edelak in second, and an unblemished nine-from-nine record on comparable going makes the surface absolutely no concern at 2m2½f.|

runners_data.name: Edelak
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton sends out the Skelton yard's in-form type (7 wins from 19 over 14 days) fresh from three consecutive wins, all on good ground over the minimum; Harry Skelton takes over and Edelak will control this from the front, though the step up from 2m on every winning run is the one question mark to resolve.|

runners_data.name: Getmetothemoon
runners_data.note: A 178-day break is a significant fitness flag for Anthony Honeyball's charge, and while Chad Bament (5) rides, Getmetothemoon's natural prominent style cannot be expressed here — crowded out by Edelak and Snatch A Glance ahead of it, it will race out of its preferred position in a role that doesn't suit.|

races.paceDynamic: Edelak is the lone confirmed front-runner in a five-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to press hard from the off, should be allowed to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Stratford. Snatch A Glance is a natural prominent type who will look to sit close to the pace, while Getmetothemoon is also a genuine prominent racer but has been mapped to midfield because the position simply cannot be filled by two horses simultaneously — Edelak and Snatch A Glance are far better placed to secure those berths. War Correspondent and Donnie Azoff will operate from the back on their natural hold-up styles, needing the pace to remain honest enough for their late efforts to land. This field holds more prominent/front-running types than the race shape can accommodate — Getmetothemoon, a true prominent racer, is most likely to be denied its natural position and forced to race out of role behind the two horses ahead of it. With Edelak controlling an uncontested, measured tempo, this race shape most strongly favours the horse stalking the leader in a position to quicken from the second flight out — the prominent profile behind the pace-setter holds the greatest tactical advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Edelak Controls, Stalker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak bowls along in front unchallenged and the race is run at a steady-to-fair clip, the horse tracking closest in second has all the tactical advantages into the final exchanges.
scenarios.body: Edelak sets the fractions from the front with Snatch A Glance in closest pursuit, and when the sprint develops from the last hurdle, the prominent stalker is optimally placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Pair Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak's steady pace is just honest enough to bring genuine closers into play in the final half-mile on quick ground.
scenarios.body: War Correspondent and Donnie Azoff, both seasoned hold-up performers with strong form on good ground, reel in the front two if tired legs appear at the last hurdle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Edelak sets a very modest tempo that turns the race into a sprint finish from which the front-runner simply isn't caught.
scenarios.body: With barely any pressure applied and the whole field bunching behind, Edelak's class and jumping accuracy on quick ground allow it to ping the last and hold on for a decisive front-running success.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos from Midfield Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the field gets shuffled and the out-of-position Getmetothemoon manages to find a clear run from the rear of the prominent group at the right moment.
scenarios.body: Getmetothemoon is a naturally forward-going type forced back and races out of its comfort zone, so this scenario relies on fortune — but a clear run from a handy position late could manufacture a surprise finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch Edelak's jumping closely — three straight wins have all come at 2m and any hesitation at hurdles over the extra four furlongs could quickly invite Snatch A Glance to close the gap and overwhelm it before the line.

Getmetothemoon returns after 178 days off and, already forced out of its natural prominent position, combination of race fitness and tactical compromise makes it a horse to monitor for signs of distress from halfway.

Donnie Azoff carries 167lbs under a claiming rider — if Isabelle Ryder struggles to fill that weight over the closing stages on quick ground, the hold-up finish War Correspondent and Donnie Azoff both need could be blunted.

Watch for Snatch A Glance's jumping fluency — nine-from-nine on similar going is elite consistency but if Fern O'Brien (5) is taken wide round Stratford's tight turns while tracking Edelak, ground could be lost at a crucial stage.

races.name: Sun Racing The Favourite Pullout Every Day Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Miss Kassiopi
runners_data.note: Won at this distance on good ground 9 days ago under Harry Skelton and arrives in-form and fresh; the confirmed pace-setter in a field that offers no challenger for the lead, giving her total control — style fit of 0.92 flags she is operating at the outer edge of her comfort zone here but her recent winning form and similar-going record of 10/15 makes her the key tactical asset.|

runners_data.name: Pure Logic
runners_data.note: Paddy Hanlon (claimer, 5lb) takes the mount for a trainer who has hit 1/11 in 14 days; prominent in style with a solid record on similar ground (9/10), but five consecutive placed-or-worse finishes without a win suggests she needs things to go perfectly from the front.|

runners_data.name: Basilette
runners_data.note: Daniel Sansom claims 3lb for Seamus Mullins, who has drawn a blank from four runners in 14 days; showed a win and a second in her last four starts and handles this type of ground well (12/15), making her the most consistent form horse in the prominent group and a serious contender if she can track the leader efficiently.|

runners_data.name: La Lolita
runners_data.note: Off 252 days — a significant fitness query for James Bowen and Gary Hanmer — but ran a win and two thirds in her last three completed starts on similar ground; a genuine hold-up type who will need the pace to collapse or an injection of stamina from the front to get into this, but the long break demands caution.|

runners_data.name: A Tickatickatiming
runners_data.note: Marc Goldstein partners this 8-year-old hold-up operator who has not won in her last five runs; the similar-going record of 7/15 is modest, and back-to-back fourth and fifth placings suggest she is consistent without being a winning force — needs a truly run race to get involved.|

runners_data.name: Quick Of The Night
runners_data.note: 39 days since last run for the Dave Roberts-trained 9-year-old, who has an excellent similar-going record (13/15) and has twice won on comparable ground; prominent in style and experienced, he brings solid credentials for this trip and surface, though age and weight (153lbs) may blunt his finishing speed.|

runners_data.name: Sadies Diamond
runners_data.note: 370 days off the track is an enormous concern for this 5-year-old, regardless of her two seconds at this sort of level; Jack Stenhouse claims 7lb and the trainer has hit 1/9 in 14 days, but the extreme absence means this is realistically a comeback run rather than a winning exercise.|

runners_data.name: Yanka Blue
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy's 5-year-old arrives 12 days fresh and is a confirmed come-from-behind horse — the map places her in mid-division because the field's hold-up contingent is too large for all to settle at the rear, meaning she is likely to find herself racing closer than her natural style demands, which compromises her chance meaningfully.|

runners_data.name: Miss Fedora
runners_data.note: Benjamin Macey (5lb claimer) rides for Nick Scholfield, who has landed 1/12 in recent days; her history contains two pulled-up or refused runs (RP/8) and her record on this type of going is patchy (8/15) — a natural hold-up mare who, like Yanka Blue, will be shuffled forward by the race shape rather than setting back as she would prefer, diluting her late-running threat.

races.paceDynamic: Miss Kassiopi is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will stride out from the front at a pace entirely of her own choosing on good-to-firm ground at Stratford. Pure Logic, Basilette, and Quick Of The Night will press forward into prominent positions behind her, creating a compact lead group rather than a strung-out field, and the steady-to-honest gallop that results should keep the race together until the final circuit. The field holds more hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear in this shape — Yanka Blue and Miss Fedora are genuine come-from-behind horses who are likely to find themselves racing closer to the pace than they would ideally prefer, compromising their ability to deliver a late challenge. This race shape strongly favours prominent-racing types who can travel efficiently in behind the leader, conserve energy through the middle stages, and produce a sustained rather than explosive finish — the profile that benefits most is a confirmed close-up racer with good form on fast ground who does not need a strong gallop to generate momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kassiopi Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Kassiopi sets a sustainable front-running gallop and the race develops into a test of jumping efficiency and stamina for the prominent brigade.
scenarios.body: Miss Kassiopi dictates every yard on terms that suit her, with Pure Logic, Basilette, and Quick Of The Night tracking in close order; when the tempo lifts from the home turn the horse best placed just off the shoulder lands the telling blow.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Kassiopi goes too hard too early and weakens from the second-last, opening a gap for runners who have been switched off in mid-division.
scenarios.body: The front group fails to sustain the tempo through the final mile and those racing in mid-division — La Lolita in particular — find themselves with ground to make up but a clear gap to aim at; the fitness edge of a well-handicapped mare running fresh off a break becomes decisive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Attrition Race
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Logic and Basilette both press Miss Kassiopi for the lead and the early fractions on firm ground become genuinely testing.
scenarios.body: The forcing pace drains the leaders, and a horse with strong stamina credentials and good jumping who has been ridden patiently through the first mile will outstay rivals on the run-in; the combination of quick ground and a high early tempo turns this into a test of raw endurance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fierce enough to cause widespread attrition and Yanka Blue or Miss Fedora — despite being forced closer than ideal — find a clear late run.
scenarios.body: Both Yanka Blue and Miss Fedora are being mapped forward of their natural territory and their redistribution means this scenario is the least likely to materialise; only a genuinely extreme gallop that destroys the prominent brigade entirely would give them the runway they need.

watchPoints.text: Miss Kassiopi dictates entirely on her own terms — if Harry Skelton allows her to bowl along without a challenge the tactical advantage she holds over every other runner in this field is decisive and she must be treated as the race-shaping danger.

La Lolita returns from 252 days off — James Bowen will need to judge the mare's fitness quickly out of the gate; if she travels sweetly into mid-division she could be a big price threat, but fitness failure on the home turn is a real risk at this stage of her preparation.

Sadies Diamond has not raced for 370 days and holds a 7lb claimer — even if she shows ability on the day, the layoff is long enough that her finishing effort could simply run out of stamina at the business end; monitor her in the market for signs of confidence from connections.

Yanka Blue and Miss Fedora are both being ridden out of their natural hold-up roles by the shape of this race — if either is seen pushing forward into a mid-division berth from early on, the late challenge that their style profile promises is already compromised before the first hurdle.

Quick Of The Night's experience and similar-going record (13/15) deserve respect at 39 days' absence — if he jumps fluently and sits handy, his stamina-based profile suits a race likely to be run at a measured but relentless Stratford gallop.
